question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(3+kx)\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=8\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=8\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when its displacement is $8\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14164351/assets/f368d2de12462a1790322edca188232bf8fafe3951facdb29b334e285807b9fe.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(3+kx)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=3+kx.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=3+kx.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (3+kx)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =3(0)+\frac{k(0)^{2}}{2}+C \\ C & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+32.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when $x=8\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+32 \\ \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{2})^{2} & =3(8)+\frac{k(8)^{2}}{2}+32 \\ 64 & =24+32k+32 \\ 32k & =8 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
